newsitem.title: LEBANON: South votes in Lebanon election. [CORRECTED 08:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: South votes in Lebanon election. [CORRECTED 08:40 GMT]

text.p: Polls opened in this southern Lebanese port city on Sunday as south Lebanon voted in the fourth round of the country's general election.
Some 552,000 voters were eligible to choose 23 deputies to the 128-member parliament.
Dozens of people waited to cast their ballots in Sidon, the major city of the south, as polling stations opened.
The election in the south, and next week's vote in the eastern Bekaa valley, will decide the distribution of the majority of seats set aside for Shi'ite Moslems in parliament.

Voters had three lists of candidates to choose from, headed by a combined list formed by two powerful Shi'ite groups -- the secular movement Amal and the pro-Iranian fundamentalist group Hizbollah (Party of God).

Amal-Hizbollah's 21 candidates were headed by Shi'ite parliament Speaker Nabih Berri, a former civil war militia chieftain, and included Bahia Hariri, sister of Sunni Moslem Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri (Corrects status of Bahia from wife.)

Hizbollah, whose guerrillas are fighting to oust Israeli troops from the south, has four candidates on the list under a deal brokered at the last minute by Syria to avert a battle between the two Shi'ite groups, which have in the past fought bitter wars in Beirut and the south.
The deal averted fears that an electoral contest between the two groups could have erupted in more fighting.

Hizbollah is seeking to maintain its strength in parliament after setbacks in the earlier rounds. It had eight deputies and four supporters in the outgoing parliament but lost two seats in the first two rounds of the election.
Hariri, who is an ally of Berri, is a sworn foe of Hizbollah but his sister was included on the list in a last-minute compromise.

Amal-Hizbollah's list is challenged by a 10-member list of leftist and communist candidates headed by Habib Saadeq, an ex-communist, and a 15-member list headed by Kamel Assad, a traditionalist Shi'ite politician and former parliament speaker.
Mount Lebanon, the north and Beirut have already voted in regional elections on the three previous Sundays. The election ends next Sunday when the eastern Bekaa valley votes.
